baseline.reason:
The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; Ran the identical /poc/run.sh (same PoC bytes/command) via run_poc on all three configured versions after applying the identical libidn2-enabling build/link additions to each.

post_intro: run_poc reports crashed=True, exit=134, with an AddressSanitizer "attempting double-free" report. First free occurs inside reuse_conn -> conn_free(old_conn) -> Curl_free_idnconverted_hostname (url.c:1649, called from url.c:3561 reuse_conn / url.c:3910 create_conn) when the freshly-created (about to be discarded) connectdata's conn_to_host.encalloc is freed — even though that identical pointer was just shallow-copied onto the kept connection (old_conn->conn_to_host.encalloc was never NULLed, only .rawalloc was, per the task's root-cause description). The second free of the same heap block happens later during the process's normal cleanup (curl_share_cleanup -> Curl_conncache_close_all_connections -> Curl_disconnect -> conn_free -> Curl_free_idnconverted_hostname, url.c:768/873) on the connection that still holds the dangling pointer. This exactly matches the described DoubleFree root cause.

pre_intro: run_poc reports crashed=False, exit=0, normal connection reuse ("Re-using existing connection #0"), no sanitizer report. Source inspection shows pre_intro's reuse_conn discards the template connection with a bare `free(conn)` (not conn_free()), so the shared host/conn_to_host pointers are never walked/freed at that point — this specific double free does not exist yet before the intro commit.

post_benign: run_poc reports crashed=False, exit=0, normal connection reuse, no sanitizer report. The fix commit introduces url_move_hostname(), which does `Curl_free_idnconverted_hostname(dest); *dest = *src; memset(src, 0, sizeof(*src));`, correctly zeroing both rawalloc and encalloc on the source side, eliminating the dangling shared pointer while preserving connection-reuse behavior.

The exact same reproducer command and inputs (/poc/run.sh, unchanged) were used across all three builds; the only difference is the target source revision itself plus the identical, uniformly-applied libidn2-enabling build/link additions.

oracle.description: No pre-existing PoC existed. Root cause: reuse_conn() in lib/url.c moves conn->conn_to_host from a freshly-created (to-be-discarded) connectdata onto the connection being kept by shallow-copying the `struct hostname`, but only NULLs old_conn->conn_to_host.rawalloc, not .encalloc. This only manifests when the IDN2 code path is exercised (host->encalloc allocated via idn2_lookup_ul), which requires libidn2 dev headers that are NOT available in this container (no idn2.h, no libidn2.so dev symlink/pkg-config, no apt/network access to install libidn2-dev, only the runtime libidn2.so.0 is present). I built a minimal idn2.h shim under /work/.idn2shim (declaring the real libidn2 ABI used by url.c: idn2_lookup_ul/idn2_check_version/idn2_strerror/idn2_free with the real flag values) plus a libidn2.so symlink to the already-installed runtime libidn2.so.0, all outside the tracked source tree. I rebuilt lib/url.c (and relinked libcurl.a / the curl binary) for pre_intro, post_intro and post_benign with -DHAVE_LIBIDN2 -DHAVE_IDN2_H -I/work/.idn2shim/include added to CPPFLAGS and -lidn2 -L/work/.idn2shim/lib added at link time, reusing each version's own already-configured sanitizer CFLAGS (each version's Makefile already carried -fsanitize=address,undefined by default) so no sanitizer coverage was lost; no tracked target source file was modified, only build flags/link inputs plus the new external stub header. /poc/run.sh: starts a local HTTP/1.1 keep-alive Python server on 127.0.0.1:8099, then runs (LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, matching curl's own setlocale(LC_ALL,"") call) `curl --connect-to orig.example:8099:café.example:8099 --resolve xn--caf-dma.example:8099:127.0.0.1 http://orig.example:8099/ http://orig.example:8099/` — two sequential requests in one invocation to the same nominal host. `café.example` is a non-ASCII conn_to_host forcing IDN2 encoding (idn2_lookup_ul allocates conn->conn_to_host.encalloc); `xn--caf-dma.example` is the pre-computed ACE/punycode form of café.example (verified by actually invoking idn2_lookup_ul with the same flags curl uses), pre-seeded into curl's DNS cache via --resolve so it connects to the local server without needing real DNS. The second request reuses the connection created by the first (exercising reuse_conn()).
